initial_plan.can_answer: partly: the data can show annual counts of pedestrians reported injured or killed in Brooklyn crashes, but cannot measure exposure-adjusted risk or all dimensions of road safety
initial_plan.metric: Annual pedestrian casualties, defined as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed
initial_plan.denominator: No exposure denominator; a count of reported pedestrian injuries and deaths
initial_plan.population: Pedestrians reported injured or killed in one-row-per-crash records with borough Brooklyn, for calendar years from 2013 onward that the file covers for a complete year
filters: include only full calendar years after checking date coverage
initial_plan.years: 2013 through the latest full calendar year represented in the file; determine the endpoint and any partial years during the data check

data_check.facts: 2013-2025 are complete calendar years; 2026 is partial (2026-01-01 through 2026-06-11). There are 473801 Brooklyn crash rows in 2013-2025, with yearly row counts in check_1.csv. There are zero Brooklyn rows with missing crash_date and zero missing number_of_pedestrians_injured or number_of_pedestrians_killed values in the selected years. The borough is an exact BROOKLYN match; missing/unknown borough values cannot enter the selected population.
data_check.meaning_and_decisions: Exclude all 2026 records (9700 Brooklyn rows through 2026-06-11) because that calendar year is partial; keep 2013-2025. Missing crash dates cannot be assigned to a year, but none occur in Brooklyn. No selected records need exclusion or special treatment for missing pedestrian injury/death counts, so include all Brooklyn crash rows in the chosen years and sum the recorded pedestrian outcomes. This remains a count of reported casualties, not an exposure-adjusted measure of risk; the row population can contain crashes with no pedestrian casualty and one crash can account for multiple casualties.
data_check.changes: The initial endpoint was set to the latest full year only after the check identified 2025 as complete and 2026 as partial; no other population or metric change.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: it measures annual counts of pedestrians reported injured or killed in Brooklyn crashes, but not exposure-adjusted risk or all dimensions of road safety
final_plan.metric: Annual count of pedestrian casualties, calculated as number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed across Brooklyn crash records
final_plan.denominator: No exposure denominator; count of reported pedestrian casualties
final_plan.population: All one-row-per-crash records with borough exactly BROOKLYN and a non-missing crash_date in calendar years 2013-2025; each pedestrian reported injured or killed contributes to the annual count
filters: exclude records with missing crash_date (none in Brooklyn)
final_plan.limitations: The file records police-reported crash outcomes, not pedestrian exposure (such as walking trips or distance), so annual counts cannot establish individual pedestrian risk or all aspects of road safety. The 2026 data only run through June 11 and are excluded. Borough is an exact recorded value and any unknown borough records are outside the Brooklyn population. No selected 2013-2025 Brooklyn records have missing pedestrian injury or death counts.
